column11: Using the New Castle County Permits & Inspections site, Identify the complete sequence of steps required to obtain a building permit for a new single-family home construction, from initial application to final certificate of occupancy.
column12:
35: End-to-End Sequence Synthesis. The response must successfully capture the macro-level sequence of the permit lifecycle, proving the model synthesized the disparate guides on the county site. Required Elements:

• Application Phase: Must mention utilizing the county's digital portals (eApply, ePlans, or eServices) to initiate the permit and upload documents.
• Construction/Inspection Phase: Must mention that once the permit is issued, construction begins and a sequence of mandatory inspections must be scheduled and passed.
• Completion Phase: Must mention that passing the final inspection AND submitting final documents results in the issuance of the Certificate of Occupancy (CO).


35: Pre-Application & Upload Requirements. The response must describe the permit workflow and include at least three of the core steps listed below, in any order. The agent has flexibility in how much detail it provides for each item, but its description must not contradict the clarifications shown in parentheses.

• Building Contractor License with Home Warranty Approval OR, if the owner-occupier is acting as their own contractor, the Owner-Occupier Affidavit and Owner-Occupier Warranty Exemption Form.
. Building Plans (MEP drawings are not required)
. Transfer Tax Forms (may mention State RTT-BPA and/or NCC Transfer Tax)
. Lines and Grades Plan (may mention "Lines and Grades" or "L&G Plan"; generic "site plan" acceptable when summarizing at a high level, provided description doesn't conflict with L&G requirements); 
. Energy Code Compliance form (REScheck or REM/Rate)
• Outside Agency Approvals (may mention DelDOT Entrance permit/approval required prior to issuance, DNREC Well/Septic, or Public Works Sewer Agreement).

20: Fees. If the response mentions fees, they must match NCC's published schedule. If no fees are mentioned, full points are awarded. Valid fees: Building Permit ($12/$1,000 valuation, min $60; $5.25/$1,000 over $1M), Certificate of Occupancy ($60 flat), Zoning Permit (10% of Building Permit Fee, $21 min/$145 max), NCC Volunteer Fire Assistance Fund (0.5% of valuation, first $1M only), Engineering Fee ($65/review if Floodplain/Wetland or L&G review required), Sewer Fees (variable, if applicable), Impact Fees (variable, may apply). Deduct all 20 points if: 1.) Response fabricates fees not in this schedule (e.g., "$15 Technology Fee"). (Note: Generic mentions of "plan review fees" are acceptable when summarizing the ePlans workflow and should not be penalized as fabricated, provided no incorrect dollar amount is attached); OR 2.) Response cites a document incorrectly associated with the fees on the county website. The following documents contain fee information:
- https://www.newcastlede.gov/205/Single-Family-Dwelling & https://www.newcastlede.gov/DocumentCenter/View/33001/Single-Family-Dwelling-Building-Permit-Requirements: Building Permit Requirements for SFD; lists Building Permit Fee, COO, Zoning, Fire Fund, Sewer, Impact, and Engineering fees
- https://www.newcastlede.gov/DocumentCenter/View/53391/Chapter-Six-01012026-unofficial-CodeOnly-web (Chapter 6 Building Code): Official comprehensive Schedule of Permit and Review Fees; confirms baseline rates, minimums, maximums, and $5.25/$1,000 rate over $1M
- https://www.newcastlede.gov/DocumentCenter/View/32992/Non-Residential-BuildingAddition-Permit-Requirements (Non-Residential Building/Addition): Same fee schedule structure and calculations for non-residential
- https://www.newcastlede.gov/DocumentCenter/View/32995/Deck-Permit-Requirements & https://www.newcastlede.gov/DocumentCenter/View/15475/Deck-Permit-Packet (Residential Deck): Same fee structure but with $142 minimum building permit fee for decks

10: Licensing & Insurance Nuance. If response mentions Worker's Compensation, General Liability Insurance, or Delaware Business License, the framing must be accurate. Correct framings: 1.) Contractor path — these are prerequisites for obtaining the Contractor License, which is then submitted with the permit application; 2.) Owner-Occupier path — these documents are not required; owner-occupiers submit an Affidavit + Warranty Exemption Form instead of a contractor license. Deduct all 20 points if response lists these as direct permit submission documents without proper context. If response doesn't mention these documents at all, full points are awarded. Response must not overstate the architect/engineer seal requirement for building plans. Correct framing: states seal "may be required" or uses conditional language, or omits the seal requirement when summarizing at a high level. Deduct all 10 points if: 1.) Response states architect/engineer signature/seal IS required, IS mandatory, or MUST be included; OR 2.) Response provides reasoning for the seal requirement that is not grounded in NCC Code Sec. 6.03.013 (which states the Code Official may accept non-professional documents for Group R-3/single-family dwellings). Fabricated explanations (e.g., "required for structural safety," "depends on square footage," or other rationale not in the code) indicate the agent did not access the correct source material.
